transcripts.transcript: One of the great potentials of AI is helping people to reduce many kinds of disadvantages or restrictions from social inequalities to physical disabilities. AI tools can provide personalised tutoring, real-time transcription, translation, and offer new possibilities of inclusion. One of the great potentials of AI is helping people to reduce many kinds of disadvantages or restrictions, from social inequalities to physical disabilities. AI tools can provide personalised tutoring, real-time transcription, translation, and offer new possibilities of inclusion. For instance, students can see their points of improvement and get tailored assignments. If dyslexia makes things harder, AI assistants can offer options to compensate. Some AI applications can even describe photos, videos and sounds for hearing and visually impaired people as an inclusive tool to enhance their perception of their environment. The new generation of translation applications can understand voice, text and images with levels of nuance that were impossible some years ago. This helps the inclusion of millions of people around the world. However, as with most things, these advantages of AI systems also come with some problems and challenges that need to be considered. While AI can help with learning and reduce disadvantages. It can't replace the empathy and understanding that humans can provide. Also for people with impairments, those who communicate in sign language rely on facial expressions and body gestures that an AI cannot provide. Along with that, descriptions for the visually impaired generated by AI can have many mistakes and should not be trusted for critical tasks. These are some of the reasons why AI is not a magic solution. Just like any other tool, it is subject to real world issues like political and economic inequalities. For example, if access to those systems is not open for everyone, only the richest will benefit. Go visit democracyAI.EU and learn more about it with more videos and a free online course.
